I am 66 and have farmed a long time, so I will keep this year simple, steady, and manageable. I only have 5 mu and a 2-person household, so I will not spread myself too thin. Cotton will stay my main crop because it fits my usual system, I know how to manage it, and with well irrigation I can support it through the key growth stages. But I will not put all 5 mu into cotton. Cotton takes more field management, more spraying, and more labor over a long season. At my age, I would rather reduce risk and labor pressure a bit, so I will put 3.5 mu into cotton and 1.5 mu into mungbean.

For cotton, I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed because I want more stable emergence and yield, but I will avoid anything too demanding. I will use moderate fertilizer, not excessive fertilizer, because too much nitrogen can make cotton grow too vegetative and harder to manage. I will plough before planting because I want a clean seedbed and better root growth at the start of the season. I will irrigate a few key times with the well, mainly around establishment, squaring, and boll setting, instead of watering too often. I will spray when needed, but I will keep the number of applications controlled. My goal is stable yield, not chasing the absolute maximum.

For mungbean, I will keep it lighter-input and easier to handle. I will use improved seed there too, because I want reliable stand establishment. Mungbean does not need as much fertilizer or water as cotton, so I will keep both modest. I will use rotary tillage for mungbean because it is enough for that crop and saves effort. I will not push pesticide use unless pressure is clear. I see mungbean as a way to spread risk, reduce labor intensity on part of the land, and still bring in useful grain from the 5 mu.
